source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 2, definition of 'legal entity'] ‘legal entity’ means a legal person created and recognised as such under Union, national or international law, which has legal personality and the capacity to act in its own name, exercise rights and be subject to obligations, or an entity which does not have legal personality as referred to in point (c) of Article 197(2) of the Financial Regulation;

[Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 (the Financial Regulation that Regulation 2021/697 cites), Article 197(2)] 2. Any of the following applicants shall be eligible for participating in a call for proposals: (a) legal persons; (b) natural persons, in so far as this is required by the nature or characteristics of the action or the objective pursued by the applicant; (c) entities which do not have legal personality under the applicable national law, provided that their representatives have the capacity to undertake legal obligations on behalf of the entities and that the entities offer guarantees for the protection of the financial interests of the Union equivalent to those offered by legal persons.

[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 11(7)] By way of derogation from paragraph 6, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with non-associated third countries, common procurement that involves a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract, and that is not established or does not have its executive management structures in the Union or in an associated country, shall be eligible for support under the Programme provided that a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product has been established between the contractor and that subcontractor prior to the date of entry into force of this Regulation.

steps.summary: A nine-digit code issued when an organisation registers on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. Free and immediate. Needed to apply for EDF and EDIP funding.

days.note: Working days are converted to calendar days at 7/5 and rounded up: 3 working days is 5 calendar days and 14 working days is 20.
days.text: Up to 14 working days on average; routine priority is 10 calendar days, emergency is 3 working days

issuers.name: Unidad de Catalogación (SECAT-OC), acting as Oficina Nacional de Catalogación (ONC) for NATO, within SDG INREID, Dirección General de Armamento y Material (DGAM), Ministerio de Defensa
issuers.notes: A new NCAGE requires an existing supply contract, and the application is submitted through the relevant Órgano de Catalogación del Ejército. No fee is published, in line with NATO policy; the word 'gratuito' does not appear on the Spanish ministry page.

steps.name: NCAGE code
steps.summary: A five-character entity identifier from the NATO codification system. Needed for NATO and NSPA supply and for stock numbers. Free of charge.

issuers.name: Oficina Nacional de Seguridad (ONS), under the Secretaria de Estado Directora del CNI
issuers.notes: Established in 1983. Portals: cni.es/oficina-nacional-de-seguridad, ons.cni.es, sede.cni.es. UNVERIFIED: processing times for the HSEM were not confirmed.

steps.name: HSEM facility security clearance (Spain)
steps.summary: The Spanish facility security clearance (Habilitación de Seguridad de Empresa), needed to handle classified information. How long it takes is not published.

issuers.name: Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (REOCE, Registro Especial de Operadores de Comercio Exterior)

steps.name: REOCE registration (Spain)
steps.summary: Spanish exporters of controlled items must be on the Special Register of Foreign Trade Operators (REOCE), before or together with the licence application. Open only to Spanish residents.

issuers.name: Subdirección General de Comercio Internacional de Material de Defensa y de Doble Uso, Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa (competent authority: Secretaría de Estado de Comercio)
issuers.notes: The interministerial regulator is the JIMDDU (Junta Interministerial Reguladora del Comercio Exterior de Material de Defensa y de Doble Uso). Legal basis: Ley 53/2007 and Real Decreto 679/2014.

steps.name: Export authorisation for dual-use or military items
steps.summary: An authorisation to export items in a controlled category. Which licence depends on whether the item is in the dual-use regime or the military regime.

issuers.name: Spanish state route: PECAL, audited through DGAM structures
issuers.notes: The Spanish equivalent of AQAP is PECAL, audited through the structures of the Dirección General de Armamento y Material rather than a commercial certification body.

steps.name: AQAP 2110 quality assurance certification
steps.priceNote: In your country the state issues this itself, so the vendor price ranges in our sources do not apply and none is shown.
steps.summary: NATO quality assurance requirements for design, development and production. Not an eligibility condition of EDF, EDIP or SAFE: it enters through individual contracts and cascades down the supply chain.
